conventions.convention: The geometry is smooth, oriented and time-oriented, with signature (-,+,+,+), the metric-selected connection, and the curvature convention inherited from def-emg-lorentzian-forms. The electromagnetic field is a smooth real two-form; no global potential is assumed.
κ=8πG_N/c⁴>0, μ₀>0, and Λ is real. T_EM=μ₀⁻¹(F_ac F_b{}^c−g_ab F_cd F^cd/4). The sourced sign is ∇_a F^{ab}=−μ₀J^b. In SI orthonormal components, e=E/c and b=B have units tesla.

The future-normal second fundamental form has the positive convention K(X,Y)=g(∇_X n,Y). The notation K=(1/2)L_n h means the initial derivative of the locally constructed induced-metric family, without a global normal-foliation assumption.

Periodic H^s uses integer orders, normalized torus measure and the GR weak-derivative norm; the Fourier-weight norm is equivalent, not declared identical. Countable Choice is assumed. Geometric components use X=L₀θ, and electromagnetic arrays use the canonical positively oriented h-orthonormal frame.

Spatial vectors e,b are obtained by raising the induced observer covectors with h. The spatial orientation satisfies vol_g=−n♭∧vol_h, and h(e×_h b,w)=vol_h(e,b,w). Abstract constrained data require a nonempty boundaryless three-manifold.

Cauchy sets meet every inextendible causal curve at exactly one parameter value. The global causal class is locally absolutely continuous with nonzero future causal derivative almost everywhere; selected escape instead uses the explicitly defined, locally finitely piecewise-C¹ path class.

Surface gravity is signed and tied to the specified generator by the ambient covector identity d(g(ξ,ξ))=−2κ_H ξ♭ on its nonzero portion. Constant rescaling ξ′=aξ gives κ′_H=aκ_H. No positivity, constancy or value at generator zeros is automatic.

Area is the supremum of compactly supported smooth cutoff-density integrals, allowing +∞ and requiring Countable Choice. Extension obstructions concern specified approaches to added points of C² nondegenerate metric extensions and curvature contractions without covariant derivatives.

load_bearing.statement: For smooth g and a smooth real two-form F, the source-free system is G_ab[g]+Λg_ab=κT_EM_ab[g,F], dF=0, d(star_g F)=0, with the stated constants, stress, orientation and initial-data conventions. No global potential or development-existence conclusion is included.

Defines the exact global causal/Cauchy conventions, null and Killing horizons, signed generator-normalized surface gravity, intrinsic section area, stationary-limit and ergoregion terminology, selected-model escape, and approached C² metric extensions with the polynomial-curvature obstruction criterion.

Under Countable Choice, for finite m≥1, open O, compact K⊆O, R≥0 and integer s≥5, S_s(K,R) consists of periodic H^s classes with their continuous representatives valued in K and norm at most R. It also specifies the length-coordinate and geometric component conventions.

Under AC_ω, integer s≥5, a smooth periodic symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family with positive A⁰, compact K⊆int K′⊆O and R≥0, bounded initial states in S_s(K,R) have a common local Sobolev solution interval, compact range and the cited norm bounds; uniqueness and H^{s−1} continuous dependence hold in the stated bounded class, and smooth data remain smooth on that interval. A coupled reduction must be verified separately.
Constrained data satisfy div_h e=div_h b=0, R(h)+τ²−|K|²=2Λ+(κ/μ₀)(|e|²+|b|²), and D^jK_ji−D_iτ=−(κ/μ₀)(e×_h b)_i, with the specified smooth or periodic high-Sobolev interpretations.
For smooth F satisfying dF=0 and ∇_aF^{ab}=−μ₀J^b, Q is symmetric and trace-free, ∇^aT_EM_ab=−F_bcJ^c, T_EM(n,n)=(|e|²+|b|²)/(2μ₀), and T_EM(n,e_i)=−(e×b)_i/μ₀.

For the specified periodic high-Sobolev data and a fixed smooth positive reference γ, the prescribed metric 1-jet with ∂₀g_ij=2K_ij, ∂₀g_00=−2tr_h K and ∂₀g_0i=h_ijQ^j has H₀=0 and first derivatives in H^s. Choosing γ=h is not licensed for finite-regularity h.

Every existing smooth source-free electrovacuum solution induces data on a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface satisfying the two Maxwell divergences and the displayed Hamiltonian and momentum constraints. This is necessary-constraint, not sufficiency or existence, theory.
For smooth A and F=dA, ∇^aF_ab=Box_g A_b−∇_b(div A)−Ric_bc A^c. Lorenz gauge removes the divergence gradient and retains the Ricci coupling.

On a coordinate image star-shaped about zero, a smooth closed two-form has the smooth potential A_a(x)=∫₀¹t x^bF_ba(tx)dt. Under AC_ω, a smooth potential near a smooth spacelike patch can locally be changed to Lorenz gauge by A′=A+dχ, preserving dA.

alerts.finding: In [L2], the item attributes to def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state the norm equality “\|u\|_{H^s}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)^s|\widehat u(k)|^2”. That definition instead inherits the weak-derivative norm from def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces and explicitly states equivalence to the Fourier-weight norm. These are not identical norms. Also [L5] says “The item file exists but is not in batch 6” about lem-emg-fixed-smooth-background-harmonic-data, although that item is explicitly in the batch-6 inventory.

[F4] says def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state “fixes” the exact Fourier-weight norm equality. Its actual definition inherits the weak-derivative norm and gives only equivalence. Consequently proof 3.1's Fourier partial-sum bound “≤R²”, with R defined as the supremum of that inherited H^s norm, is not justified with constant one. A Fourier mode with frequency (1,1,0) distinguishes the two norms for s≥2. Norm-equivalence constants recover the boundedness argument, but the exact citation and bound need correction.

The Statement says the draft electrovacuum definition's “draft status and manifest omission are recorded in [L1]”. In fact [L1] says “The item file is listed in the batch-6 manifest”, agreeing with the current batch-6 inventory. The manifest-omission wording is stale.

Definition (e) displays H⁺(S)=D⁺(S)\I⁻(D⁺(S)) but glosses it as points “that are not chronologically preceded by any point of D⁺(S)”. Membership in I⁻(D⁺(S)) means chronologically preceding some point of D⁺(S), so this prose reverses the chronological direction of the displayed formula.

seams_checked.note: The source-free system, stress signs, necessary constraints, fixed smooth-background harmonic jet and conditional periodic solver are faithfully used. CP02 supplies its own C¹ stress extension rather than silently strengthening CP01's smooth theorem. However, the coupled-evolution and continuation items misquote the Sobolev norm as exactly the Fourier-weight norm; stale batch-inventory wording also remains. These discrepancies are routed in alerts.

RN curvature and KN invariant consumers use precisely the specified-approach C² nondegenerate extension obstruction. Their divergence arguments concern polynomial curvature contractions along approaching sequences and make no completeness or distributional-source inference.

Horizon consumers verify null conormals, nonzero Killing generators, ambient signed surface-gravity normalization and intrinsic section area. Ergosurface terminology remains separate from horizons. Escape consumers use the specified locally finitely piecewise-C¹ path class and relative selected-model boundary; the charged-ring consumer uses the exact approached-extension obstruction.
